title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: CLYDE'S SECRET
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Clyde Ferris, a forklift mechanic in Sioux City, Iowa.
Big guy. Quiet guy.
Every day at lunch, he sang in his pickup with the windows rolled up.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE FLYER
segments.quote: If you hear a voice within you say you cannot paint, then by all means paint, and that voice will be silenced.
segments.author: Vincent van Gogh
lines: One day a flyer at the hardware store said: Barbershop quartet needs a bass. Tuesdays.
A voice in his head said, You? Sing? Ha.
Then he remembered his mom's fridge magnet, from the painter Vincent van Gogh:
If you hear a voice within you say you cannot paint, then by all means paint, and that voice will be silenced.
Clyde tore off the phone number.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE BASEMENT
segments.quote: Because I think I am making progress.
segments.author: Pablo Casals
lines: The other three were retired. Earl sang lead.
Clyde was flat on every song.
Earl told him the great cellist Pablo Casals still practiced in his nineties. Asked why, he said:
Because I think I am making progress.
So Clyde practiced in the truck every lunch. A little better each week.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: TOO LOUD
segments.quote: Know how to listen, and you will profit even from those who talk badly.
segments.author: Plutarch
lines: Then he got proud, and loud. The other three disappeared.
Earl held up an old book by Plutarch, a Greek writer:
Know how to listen, and you will profit even from those who talk badly.
Or sing badly, Earl added, pointing at himself.
So Clyde sang softer and listened. The chord rang. Goosebumps.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE PANCAKES
segments.quote: In any case you mustn't confuse a single failure with a final defeat.
segments.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
lines: Their first show was the Fourth of July pancake breakfast at the VFW.
Clyde started in the wrong key. A toddler clapped anyway.
Clyde wanted to quit. Herb, the baritone, quoted F. Scott Fitzgerald:
In any case you mustn't confuse a single failure with a final defeat.
Next Tuesday, Clyde showed up early. With pancakes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: LOST VOICE
segments.quote: Just don't give up trying to do what you really want to do.
segments.author: Ella Fitzgerald
lines: The night before the state contest in Des Moines, Earl lost his voice.
Clyde would have to sing lead. His hands shook.
Earl wrote a napkin note from the jazz singer Ella Fitzgerald. No relation to Scott:
Just don't give up trying to do what you really want to do.
Clyde put the napkin in his pocket and learned the lead by midnight.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE STAGE
segments.quote: Music washes away from the soul the dust of everyday life.
segments.author: Berthold Auerbach
lines: On stage, Clyde saw half the plant in the third row.
Before they sang, Earl whispered a line from the German writer Berthold Auerbach:
Music washes away from the soul the dust of everyday life.
Clyde sang like a man with nothing to hide. They took third place.
Now he sings at lunch with the windows down.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Start anyway. Practice. Listen. Get back up. Keep trying. Sing it out.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Start anyway. Practice a little. Listen. Get back up. Keep trying. And sing it out.
Me, I only sing in the shower. The neighbors have asked me to take baths.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
